key_insight: A fully discrete finite element scheme for Kirchhoff-type equations achieves optimal spatial accuracy and second-order time accuracy, while exactly preserving discrete energy for homogeneous problems with constant coefficients.
engineering_relevance: The method supports accurate simulation of nonlinear structural dynamics with nonlocal stiffness effects, with conservation guarantees in the constant-coefficient, homogeneous setting.
method: Conforming finite elements of arbitrary polynomial degree p in two spatial dimensions.
Picard iteration for the nonlinearity, supported by well-definedness and convergence analysis.
evidence_signal: Manufactured-solution experiments reproduce second-order temporal convergence and spatial L² accuracy of order h^(p+1), consistent with the theoretical error bounds.
watch_item: Exact discrete energy conservation applies to the exactly solved scheme with constant coefficients and no forcing; finite Picard tolerances may introduce conservation errors.
paper_title: Conservative Finite Element Methods for Kirchhoff-Type Equations
